name: ProSelect
tagline: Desktop presentation and sales software for photographers: show images to clients, mock them up on their walls at real size, and build the order.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The part clients actually react to, big images on a dark screen, side by side comparison, favorites, and a wall mock-up with a frame at true size, is a legitimate one-shot build. Real world scaling is just arithmetic once the client tells you their sofa is 84 inches wide, and a frame catalog is a JSON file you type once. Where the DIY version falls apart is everything downstream: album and book layout, package and discount pricing logic, lab ordering, invoicing, and the years of hardening that keep the app from freezing while someone is holding a credit card. Also worth noting that this runs live in front of a paying client, which is the least forgiving environment a homemade app can be dropped into. Build it for the viewing and mock-up loop, keep the ordering in your existing invoicing tool.
coreLoopDIY: A local fullscreen image presenter that compares shots, stars favorites, and composites selected images onto a photo of the client's wall at correct real-world size inside a chosen frame and mat.
requirements: Node 20 and a local folder of high-res client images
A photo of the client's wall plus one known measurement in it for scale
A hand-written JSON price and frame catalog
whatYouLose: Color-managed, calibrated display so the screen preview matches what the lab prints
Lab and ROES style ordering integration, so orders leave your app as a CSV instead of a print job
Album and book design with spread templates and auto layout
Package, bundle, and discount pricing logic that has been tuned by thousands of studios
Battle-tested stability during a live sales session, where a crash costs real money
moatNotes: Frame moulding catalogs and lab product lists are boring, proprietary, and constantly changing, which is exactly the kind of data nobody wants to maintain themselves.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the software is sitting between a photographer and the moment a family decides to spend two thousand dollars. At that moment you want something that has survived a decade of other people's sales appointments, that renders a 30x40 canvas over the client's fireplace without stuttering, and that turns the yes into an order the lab will accept without retyping. A weekend build can show pictures beautifully. It cannot absorb the cost of being wrong about a frame size or freezing mid-pitch, and the frame and product catalogs alone are more ongoing maintenance than most photographers want to own.
notes: The viewing and wall mock-up loop is a weekend; the ordering pipeline is the actual product.
prompt:
Build a local desktop-style client image presentation and wall mock-up app for a photographer. Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript on the front end, a small Node 20 Express server for reading local image folders and writing session files. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics. Everything runs with `npm install && npm run dev` and opens in a browser on localhost.

In scope:
- Server reads a folder path from IMAGE_DIR in .env, lists JPEG/PNG files, serves full-size and cached thumbnails (sharp).
- Presentation view: fullscreen, near-black background, one image fills the screen, arrow keys and space to navigate, no visible chrome unless the mouse moves.
- Compare mode: show 2, 3, or 4 selected images side by side with equal heights, keyboard shortcuts to swap any slot.
- Favoriting: key press stars or rejects the current image; a filmstrip at the bottom shows stars; filter to starred only.
- Room view: client uploads or drags in a photo of their wall. User draws a line over a known object and types its real width in inches to set a pixels-per-inch scale. Then place any starred image on the wall as a composited rectangle at a chosen print size, with drag to move, and a subtle drop shadow.
- Frame and mat catalog loaded from a local frames.json file: name, moulding width in inches, mat width in inches, border color or texture image. Rendering must add moulding and mat outside the image area so the overall footprint is physically correct.
- Size picker driven by products.json: print sizes with prices. Show the total footprint in inches and the price next to each option.
- Order summary panel: list of chosen image + size + frame + price, running subtotal, export to CSV and a plain printable HTML summary. No payments, no tax engine.
- Sessions persist to a JSON file per client in ./sessions so you can reopen an appointment.

Out of scope, do not build: album or book layout, lab ordering integrations, invoicing, email delivery, client web galleries, ICC color management, user auth, any hosted component.

Requirements: handle 40 megapixel files without blocking the UI (preload neighbors, use thumbnails in the filmstrip). Presentation view must never show a loading spinner on next image. Ship frames.json and products.json with three plausible sample entries each and a README explaining how to edit them.
